result:
I fixed both findings. One part needs you: I couldn't write `.github/` (the sandbox makes it read-only), so the workflow change is only in the staged `deploy/ci/ci.yml`. Install it with `cp deploy/ci/ci.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml`. The handback is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG1/round-3/T-DG1-DEVOPS3-devops-engineer.md`, with exact commands, output and sha256 checksums. Nothing is committed.

**F-DG1-116: more ways to weaken the gate step.** `deploy/scripts/check-ci-needs.mjs` now rejects anything not on an explicit allow-list:
- **Workflow level:** no `defaults:` or `env:` blocks.
- **`delivery-gates` job:** only `name`, `runs-on`, `steps`, `permissions`, `timeout-minutes` and `continue-on-error: false`. No job `env`, `defaults`, `container`, `services`, `if` and so on.
- **Gate job steps:** only pinned checkout and setup-node actions plus the validate step. No other `run:` step, which also closes the route of writing to `$GITHUB_ENV` or editing the validator before it runs.
- **Any step anywhere that runs `validate.mjs`:** only `name`, `id` and `run`. So `env:` (`NODE_OPTIONS`), `shell:` and `working-directory:` are rejected.

The existing F-DG1-107 checks are unchanged.

The self-test gains 11 failing cases (N19–N29) and 2 passing ones. N19–N22 are the four round-2 vectors exactly as the reviewer wrote them. Run against the old checker from `HEAD`, those 11 cases fail with "expected exit 1, got 0" (24 pass, 11 fail), so the old checker accepted every one of them. With the new checker all of them pass.

**F-DG1-108/203: unpinned keycloak image in CI.**
- **New guard:** `pin-images.mjs --resolve --missing` looks up only images that still have no digest. It never touches the pinned ones, and when nothing is missing it doesn't contact any registry.
- **CI step:** the `images` job now runs `--resolve --missing` then `--apply` before `--check`. It also saves the resolved lock to the `stack-evidence` artifact so IT can review and commit the pin.
- **Tests:** a stub `docker` covers three cases: a runner that can reach quay.io (keycloak gets pinned and `--check` passes), one that can't (BLOCKED, digest stays empty, `--check` fails), and a nothing-missing no-op. A fourth test checks the step order in the workflow.

`deploy/images.lock.json` is unchanged and no digest was made up. As expected, `node deploy/scripts/pin-images.mjs --check` on the committed code still exits 1 on keycloak anywhere without quay.io access. That is the disclosed D-049 residual: keycloak is a test-only login server, and the production images are already pinned.

**Checks run (offline):**
- `node --test deploy/scripts/tests/*.test.mjs`: 48 of 48 pass.
- `node deploy/scripts/check-ci-needs.mjs`: exit 0 on both the installed and the staged workflow.
- `pin-images --check`: exit 1 on keycloak, as expected here.
- Both workflow copies parse as valid YAML.
- prettier and eslint pass on the changed files.

**Not run:**
- The real GitHub Actions `images` job is BLOCKED: there's no network or runner here, so the live quay.io lookup is only shown with the stub.
- The full-repo `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm lint` weren't run, only the changed files.

The new rules are deliberately strict. Any future workflow-level `env`/`defaults`, or a new key on the gate job or its steps, will fail the checker until someone reviews it and adds it to the allow-list.
